sanskrit: tṛptāś ca subhṛśaṃ tena sukhitā vigatajvarāḥ nṛtyantaś ca hasantaś ca yathā svargajitas tathā
english: Sated to the full by that blood, contented and freed of fever, they danced and laughed like those who had conquered heaven.

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya ṛṣayaḥ satapodhanāḥ tīrthayātrāṃ samājagmuḥ sarasvatyāṃ mahīpate
english: After some time, O lord of earth, the sages rich in austerity came together on a pilgrimage to the sacred fords along the Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: teṣu sarveṣu tīrtheṣu āplutya munipuṃgavāḥ prāpya prītiṃ parāṃ cāpi tapolubdhā viśāradāḥ prayayur hi tato rājan yena tīrthaṃ hi tat tathā
english: Bathing at all those fords, those bulls among sages—learned men eager for further penance—won the highest joy; and then, O king, they proceeded onward to that very ford.

sanskrit: athāgamya mahābhāgās tat tīrthaṃ dāruṇaṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā toyaṃ sarasvatyāḥ śoṇitena pariplutam pīyamānaṃ ca rakṣobhir bahubhir nṛpasattama
english: Then, O best of kings, when those greatly blessed ones reached that dreadful ford, they beheld the water of the Sarasvatī flooded with blood and being drunk by a host of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā rākṣasān rājan munayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ paritrāṇe sarasvatyāḥ paraṃ yatnaṃ pracakrire
english: Seeing those rākṣasas, O king, the sages of firm vows made the utmost effort to rescue the Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: te tu sarve mahābhāgāḥ samāgamya mahāvratāḥ āhūya saritāṃ śreṣṭhām idaṃ vacanam abruvan
english: Those greatly blessed ones, men of mighty vows, all gathered together, and summoning the best of rivers, they spoke these words.

sanskrit: kāraṇaṃ brūhi kalyāṇi kimarthaṃ te hrado hy ayam evam ākulatāṃ yātaḥ śrutvā pāsyāmahe vayam
english: "Tell us the cause, O blessed one: why has this pool of yours fallen into such a troubled state? When we have heard it, we shall set it right."

sanskrit: tataḥ sā sarvam ācaṣṭa yathāvṛttaṃ pravepatī duḥkhitām atha tāṃ dṛṣṭvā ta ūcur vai tapodhanāḥ
english: Then, trembling, she told them all that had come to pass; and beholding her in her grief, those sages rich in penance spoke.

sanskrit: kāraṇaṃ śrutam asmābhiḥ śāpaś caiva śruto 'naghe kariṣyanti tu yat prāptaṃ sarva eva tapodhanāḥ
english: "We have heard the cause, O sinless one, and we have heard of the curse as well; now all these sages rich in penance shall do what is needful."

sanskrit: evam uktvā saricchreṣṭhām ūcus te 'tha parasparam vimocayāmahe sarve śāpād etāṃ sarasvatīm
english: Having spoken thus to the best of rivers, they said one to another, "Let us all release this Sarasvatī from the curse."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu vacanād eva prakṛtisthā sarasvatī prasannasalilā jajñe yathā pūrvaṃ tathaiva hi vimuktā ca saricchreṣṭhā vibabhau sā yathā purā
english: At their word alone the Sarasvatī was restored to her natural state, her waters grown clear as before; and freed, that best of rivers shone forth as she had of old.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā toyaṃ sarasvatyā munibhis tais tathā kṛtam kṛtāñjalīs tato rājan rākṣasāḥ kṣudhayārditāḥ ūcus tān vai munīn sarvān kṛpāyuktān punaḥ punaḥ
english: Beholding the water of the Sarasvatī thus made pure by those sages, the rākṣasas, tormented by hunger, O king, with hands joined in reverence, spoke again and again to all those merciful sages.

sanskrit: vayaṃ hi kṣudhitāś caiva dharmād dhīnāś ca śāśvatāt na ca naḥ kāmakāro 'yaṃ yad vayaṃ pāpakāriṇaḥ
english: "We are famished, and fallen away from the eternal law; yet this is no doing of our own desire, that we have become workers of evil."

sanskrit: yuṣmākaṃ cāprasādena duṣkṛtena ca karmaṇā pakṣo 'yaṃ vardhate 'smākaṃ yataḥ sma brahmarākṣasāḥ
english: "It is through your displeasure and through evil deeds that our number swells; for from such causes do we become brahma-rākṣasas."

sanskrit: evaṃ hi vaiśyaśūdrāṇāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ tathaiva ca ye brāhmaṇān pradviṣanti te bhavantīha rākṣasāḥ
english: "For thus it is: among vaiśyas and śūdras, and among kṣatriyas likewise, those who hate the brāhmaṇas become rākṣasas here."

sanskrit: ācāryam ṛtvijaṃ caiva guruṃ vṛddhajanaṃ tathā prāṇino ye 'vamanyante te bhavantīha rākṣasāḥ yoṣitāṃ caiva pāpānāṃ yonidoṣeṇa vardhate
english: "Those creatures who slight the teacher, the officiating priest, the elder, and the aged become rākṣasas here; and the breed grows too through the taint in the wombs of sinful women."

sanskrit: tat kurudhvam ihāsmākaṃ kāruṇyaṃ dvijasattamāḥ śaktā bhavantaḥ sarveṣāṃ lokānām api tāraṇe
english: "Therefore show us your compassion here, O best of the twice-born; you have the power to deliver even all the worlds."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ te munayaḥ śrutvā tuṣṭuvus tāṃ mahānadīm mokṣārthaṃ rakṣasāṃ teṣām ūcuḥ prayatamānasāḥ
english: Hearing their plea, those sages praised that great river; and for the deliverance of those rākṣasas they spoke, their minds intent.

sanskrit: kṣutakīṭāvapannaṃ ca yac cocchiṣṭāśitaṃ bhavet keśāvapannam ādhūtam ārugṇam api yad bhavet śvabhiḥ saṃspṛṣṭam annaṃ ca bhāgo 'sau rakṣasām iha
english: "Food into which an insect has fallen, or that is left as another's leavings, into which a hair has dropped, or that is shaken about, or sickened, or touched by dogs—that is the portion of the rākṣasas here."

sanskrit: tasmāj jñātvā sadā vidvān etāny annāni varjayet rākṣasānnam asau bhuṅkte yo bhuṅkte hy annam īdṛśam
english: "Therefore the wise man, knowing this, should ever shun such food; for whoever eats food of that kind eats the food of rākṣasas."

sanskrit: śodhayitvā tatas tīrtham ṛṣayas te tapodhanāḥ mokṣārthaṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca nadīṃ tāṃ pratyacodayan
english: Then, having purified that ford, those sages rich in penance urged the river onward for the deliverance of the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: maharṣīṇāṃ mataṃ jñātvā tataḥ sā saritāṃ varā aruṇām ānayām āsa svāṃ tanuṃ puruṣarṣabha
english: Knowing the will of the great sages, that best of rivers, O bull among men, brought forth her own stream as the Aruṇā.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ te rākṣasāḥ snātvā tanūs tyaktvā divaṃ gatāḥ aruṇāyāṃ mahārāja brahmahatyāpahā hi sā
english: Bathing in her, those rākṣasas cast off their bodies and went to heaven; for the Aruṇā, O great king, washes away the slaying of a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: etam artham abhijñāya devarājaḥ śatakratuḥ tasmiṃs tīrthavare snātvā vimuktaḥ pāpmanā kila
english: Knowing this virtue of it, the king of the gods, Lord of a Hundred Sacrifices, bathed at that excellent ford and was freed, indeed, from his sin.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kimarthaṃ bhagavāñ śakro brahmahatyām avāptavān katham asmiṃś ca tīrthe vai āplutyākalmaṣo 'bhavat
english: Janamejaya said: For what cause did the blessed Śakra incur the guilt of slaying a brāhmaṇa, and how, by bathing at this ford, did he become free of stain?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śṛṇuṣvaitad upākhyānaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ janeśvara yathā bibheda samayaṃ namucer vāsavaḥ purā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hear this tale as it came to pass, O lord of men—how of old Vāsava broke his compact with Namuci.

sanskrit: namucir vāsavād bhītaḥ sūryaraśmiṃ samāviśat tenendraḥ sakhyam akarot samayaṃ cedam abravīt
english: Namuci, in dread of Vāsava, entered into a ray of the sun; with him Indra made friendship, and spoke this compact.

sanskrit: nārdreṇa tvā na śuṣkeṇa na rātrau nāpi vāhani vadhiṣyāmy asuraśreṣṭha sakhe satyena te śape
english: "Not with anything wet nor dry, not by night nor yet by day shall I slay you, O best of asuras; I swear it to you, my friend, in truth."

sanskrit: evaṃ sa kṛtvā samayaṃ sṛṣṭvā nīhāram īśvaraḥ cicchedāsya śiro rājann apāṃ phenena vāsavaḥ
english: Having made this compact, the Lord conjured up a mist, and with the foam of the waters, O king, Vāsava severed his head.

sanskrit: tac chiro namuceś chinnaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ śakram anvayāt he mitrahan pāpa iti bruvāṇaṃ śakram antikāt
english: That severed head of Namuci followed close behind Śakra, crying out hard upon him, "O slayer of a friend! O sinner!"

sanskrit: evaṃ sa śirasā tena codyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ pitāmahāya saṃtapta evam arthaṃ nyavedayat
english: Thus driven on again and again by that head, sorely tormented, he laid the matter before the Grandsire.

sanskrit: tam abravīl lokagurur aruṇāyāṃ yathāvidhi iṣṭvopaspṛśa devendra brahmahatyāpahā hi sā
english: The Teacher of the worlds said to him: "At the Aruṇā, O lord of gods, offer sacrifice according to rule and touch its waters; for it washes away the slaying of a brāhmaṇa."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa sarasvatyāḥ kuñje vai janamejaya iṣṭvā yathāvad balabhid aruṇāyām upāspṛśat
english: Thus addressed, O Janamejaya, the Slayer of Bala, in a bower of the Sarasvatī, sacrificed as ordained and touched the waters of the Aruṇā.

sanskrit: sa muktaḥ pāpmanā tena brahmahatyākṛtena ha jagāma saṃhṛṣṭamanās tridivaṃ tridaśeśvaraḥ
english: Freed of that sin wrought by the slaying of a brāhmaṇa, the lord of the thirty gods went to heaven with gladdened heart.

sanskrit: śiras tac cāpi namuces tatraivāplutya bhārata lokān kāmadughān prāptam akṣayān rājasattama
english: And that head of Namuci too, bathing there, O Bhārata, attained the worlds that grant every wish and never wane, O best of kings.

sanskrit: tatrāpy upaspṛśya balo mahātmā; dattvā ca dānāni pṛthagvidhāni avāpya dharmaṃ param āryakarmā; jagāma somasya mahat sa tīrtham
english: There too the great-souled Bala touched the waters, and bestowing gifts of many kinds, that doer of noble deeds won the highest merit; then he went on to the great ford of Soma.

sanskrit: yatrāyajad rājasūyena somaḥ; sākṣāt purā vidhivat pārthivendra atrir dhīmān vipramukhyo babhūva; hotā yasmin kratumukhye mahātmā
english: There, O lord of kings, Soma himself had of old performed the Rājasūya sacrifice duly; and at that foremost of rites the wise Atri, chief of brāhmaṇas, that great soul, served as the invoking priest.

sanskrit: yasyānte 'bhūt sumahān dānavānāṃ; daiteyānāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca devaiḥ sa saṃgrāmas tārakākhyaḥ sutīvro; yatra skandas tārakākhyaṃ jaghāna
english: At whose close there arose a tremendous battle—the gods against the dānavas, the daityas, and the rākṣasas—the fierce war called Tāraka's, wherein Skanda slew the asura named Tāraka.

sanskrit: senāpatyaṃ labdhavān devatānāṃ; mahāseno yatra daityāntakartā sākṣāc cātra nyavasat kārttikeyaḥ; sadā kumāro yatra sa plakṣarājaḥ
english: There Mahāsena, slayer of the daityas, won the command of the armies of the gods; and there in person dwelt Kārttikeya—where the youth Kumāra abides forever, that lord of the Plakṣa king.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca sarasvatyāḥ prabhāvo 'yam uktas te dvijasattama kumārasyābhiṣekaṃ tu brahman vyākhyātum arhasi
english: Janamejaya said: This glory of the Sarasvatī you have told, O best of the twice-born; but now, O brāhmaṇa, you ought to relate the consecration of Kumāra.

sanskrit: yasmin kāle ca deśe ca yathā ca vadatāṃ vara yaiś cābhiṣikto bhagavān vidhinā yena ca prabhuḥ
english: At what time and in what place, and in what manner, O best of speakers, and by whom and by what rite the blessed lord was consecrated—

sanskrit: skando yathā ca daityānām akarot kadanaṃ mahat tathā me sarvam ācakṣva paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: and how Skanda wrought the great slaughter of the daityas—tell me all of it, for my curiosity is very great.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kuruvaṃśasya sadṛśam idaṃ kautūhalaṃ tava harṣam utpādayaty etad vaco me janamejaya
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: This curiosity of yours is worthy of the line of Kuru; this word of yours gives me joy, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: hanta te kathayiṣyāmi śṛṇvānasya janādhipa abhiṣekaṃ kumārasya prabhāvaṃ ca mahātmanaḥ
english: Come then, I shall tell you, as you listen, O ruler of men, the consecration of Kumāra and the glory of that great soul.

sanskrit: tejo māheśvaraṃ skannam agnau prapatitaṃ purā tat sarvabhakṣo bhagavān nāśakad dagdhum akṣayam
english: Of old, the seed of Maheśvara, spilled and fallen into the fire—that imperishable splendour the blessed All-devourer could not consume.

sanskrit: tenāsīdati tejasvī dīptimān havyavāhanaḥ na caiva dhārayām āsa garbhaṃ tejomayaṃ tadā
english: By it the bearer of oblations grew exceedingly bright and blazing; yet he could not hold that embryo made of splendour.

sanskrit: sa gaṅgām abhisaṃgamya niyogād brahmaṇaḥ prabhuḥ garbham āhitavān divyaṃ bhāskaropamatejasam
english: Then the lord, at the command of Brahmā, drew near to Gaṅgā and placed in her the divine embryo, splendid as the sun.

sanskrit: atha gaṅgāpi taṃ garbham asahantī vidhāraṇe utsasarja girau ramye himavaty amarārcite
english: But Gaṅgā too, unable to bear the burden of that embryo, cast it off upon the lovely mountain Himavat, honoured by the immortals.

sanskrit: sa tatra vavṛdhe lokān āvṛtya jvalanātmajaḥ dadṛśur jvalanākāraṃ taṃ garbham atha kṛttikāḥ
english: There the son of the Fire grew, filling the worlds; and then the Kṛttikās beheld that embryo in the likeness of flame.

sanskrit: śarastambe mahātmānam analātmajam īśvaram mamāyam iti tāḥ sarvāḥ putrārthinyo 'bhicakramuḥ
english: That great soul, the son of Fire, the lord, lying in a thicket of reeds—they all approached him, each longing for a son, crying, "He is mine!"

sanskrit: tāsāṃ viditvā bhāvaṃ taṃ mātṝṇāṃ bhagavān prabhuḥ prasnutānāṃ payaḥ ṣaḍbhir vadanair apibat tadā
english: Knowing that longing of those mothers, the blessed lord then drank with six mouths the milk that flowed from them.

sanskrit: taṃ prabhāvaṃ samālakṣya tasya bālasya kṛttikāḥ paraṃ vismayam āpannā devyo divyavapurdharāḥ
english: Beholding that power of the child, the Kṛttikās, goddesses bearing forms divine, fell into the utmost amazement.

sanskrit: yatrotsṛṣṭaḥ sa bhagavān gaṅgayā girimūrdhani sa śailaḥ kāñcanaḥ sarvaḥ saṃbabhau kurusattama
english: There, on the mountain's crest, where the blessed one was cast off by Gaṅgā, that whole peak turned to gold and shone, O best of the Kurus.

sanskrit: vardhatā caiva garbheṇa pṛthivī tena rañjitā ataś ca sarve saṃvṛttā girayaḥ kāñcanākarāḥ
english: By that growing embryo the earth itself was made radiant, and thus all the mountains became mines of gold.

sanskrit: kumāraś ca mahāvīryaḥ kārttikeya iti smṛtaḥ gāṅgeyaḥ pūrvam abhavan mahāyogabalānvitaḥ
english: And Kumāra of mighty valour came to be known as Kārttikeya; first he was Gāṅgeya, the son of Gaṅgā, endowed with the great power of yoga.

sanskrit: sa devas tapasā caiva vīryeṇa ca samanvitaḥ vavṛdhe 'tīva rājendra candravat priyadarśanaḥ
english: That god, possessed of penance and of valour, grew exceedingly, O lord of kings, fair to look upon as the moon.

sanskrit: sa tasmin kāñcane divye śarastambe śriyā vṛtaḥ stūyamānas tadā śete gandharvair munibhis tathā
english: There in that golden, divine thicket of reeds, wrapped in splendour, he lay while gandharvas and sages sang his praises.

sanskrit: tathainam anvanṛtyanta devakanyāḥ sahasraśaḥ divyavāditranṛttajñāḥ stuvantyaś cārudarśanāḥ
english: And so before him danced the daughters of the gods by the thousand—skilled in heavenly music and dance, lovely to behold, hymning his praise.

sanskrit: anvāste ca nadī devaṃ gaṅgā vai saritāṃ varā dadhāra pṛthivī cainaṃ bibhratī rūpam uttamam
english: The river Gaṅgā, best of streams, waited upon the god, and the earth, taking on her fairest form, bore him up.

sanskrit: jātakarmādikās tasya kriyāś cakre bṛhaspatiḥ vedaś cainaṃ caturmūrtir upatasthe kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Bṛhaspati performed for him the birth-rite and the rest of the ceremonies; and the Veda in fourfold form attended him with hands joined in reverence.

sanskrit: dhanurvedaś catuṣpādaḥ śastragrāmaḥ sasaṃgrahaḥ tatrainaṃ samupātiṣṭhat sākṣād vāṇī ca kevalā
english: The science of archery in its four divisions, the whole array of weapons with their lore, and Speech herself, all alone, in person stood there to serve him.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa mahāvīryaṃ devadevam umāpatim śailaputryā sahāsīnaṃ bhūtasaṃghaśatair vṛtam
english: He beheld the god of mighty valour, the god of gods, the lord of Umā, seated together with the Daughter of the Mountain and surrounded by hundreds of throngs of spirits.

sanskrit: nikāyā bhūtasaṃghānāṃ paramādbhutadarśanāḥ vikṛtā vikṛtākārā vikṛtābharaṇadhvajāḥ
english: The hosts of those spirit-throngs were most wondrous to look upon—misshapen, of distorted form, with distorted ornaments and banners.

sanskrit: vyāghrasiṃharkṣavadanā biḍālamakarānanāḥ vṛṣadaṃśamukhāś cānye gajoṣṭravadanās tathā
english: Some had the faces of tigers, lions, and bears; some the visages of cats and crocodiles; others bore the muzzles of bulls and rats, and yet others the faces of elephants and camels.

sanskrit: ulūkavadanāḥ ke cid gṛdhragomāyudarśanāḥ krauñcapārāvatanibhair vadanai rāṅkavair api
english: Some had the faces of owls, some the look of vultures and jackals, and some with faces like the krauñca and the dove, or like the antelope.

sanskrit: śvāvicchalyakagodhānāṃ kharaiḍakagavāṃ tathā sadṛśāni vapūṃṣy anye tatra tatra vyadhārayan
english: Others, here and there, bore bodies resembling those of porcupines, hedgehogs, and monitor lizards, of asses, rams, and cattle.

sanskrit: ke cic chailāmbudaprakhyāś cakrālātagadāyudhāḥ ke cid añjanapuñjābhāḥ ke cic chvetācalaprabhāḥ
english: Some were like mountains or rain-clouds, armed with discus, firebrand, and mace; some shone like heaps of collyrium, and some gleamed like a white mountain.

sanskrit: saptamātṛgaṇāś caiva samājagmur viśāṃ pate sādhyā viśve 'tha maruto vasavaḥ pitaras tathā
english: The bands of the Seven Mothers too came together, O lord of peoples, and the Sādhyas, the Viśvedevas, the Maruts, the Vasus, and the fathers as well.

sanskrit: rudrādityās tathā siddhā bhujagā dānavāḥ khagāḥ brahmā svayaṃbhūr bhagavān saputraḥ saha viṣṇunā
english: The Rudras and Ādityas, the siddhas, serpents, dānavas, and birds; and the blessed self-born Brahmā with his sons, together with Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: śakras tathābhyayād draṣṭuṃ kumāravaram acyutam nāradapramukhāś cāpi devagandharvasattamāḥ
english: Śakra too came to look upon that noblest and imperishable Kumāra, as did the best of the divine gandharvas, led by Nārada.

sanskrit: devarṣayaś ca siddhāś ca bṛhaspatipurogamāḥ ṛbhavo nāma varadā devānām api devatāḥ te 'pi tatra samājagmur yāmā dhāmāś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: The divine sages and the siddhas, led by Bṛhaspati, and the boon-giving ones called Ṛbhus, gods even of the gods—they too gathered there, the Yāmas and the Dhāmas, all of them.

sanskrit: sa tu bālo 'pi bhagavān mahāyogabalānvitaḥ abhyājagāma deveśaṃ śūlahastaṃ pinākinam
english: And the blessed one, though but a child, endowed with the great power of yoga, drew near to the lord of gods, the trident-bearer, the wielder of the Pināka.

sanskrit: tam āvrajantam ālakṣya śivasyāsīn manogatam yugapac chailaputryāś ca gaṅgāyāḥ pāvakasya ca
english: As they marked him drawing near, a thought arose at one and the same moment in the minds of Śiva, of the Daughter of the Mountain, of Gaṅgā, and of the Fire.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu pūrvam ayaṃ bālo gauravād abhyupaiṣyati api mām iti sarveṣāṃ teṣām āsīn manogatam
english: "To which of us first will this child come out of reverence—will it be to me?"—such was the thought in the mind of each of them.

sanskrit: teṣām etam abhiprāyaṃ caturṇām upalakṣya saḥ yugapad yogam āsthāya sasarja vividhās tanūḥ
english: Perceiving this intent of those four, he at once resorted to yoga and put forth bodies of various kinds.

sanskrit: tato 'bhavac caturmūrtiḥ kṣaṇena bhagavān prabhuḥ skandaḥ śākho viśākhaś ca naigameṣaś ca pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: Then in an instant the blessed lord became fourfold in form: Skanda, Śākha, and Viśākha, and Naigameṣa behind them.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa kṛtvā hy ātmānaṃ caturdhā bhagavān prabhuḥ yato rudras tataḥ skando jagāmādbhutadarśanaḥ
english: Thus having made himself fourfold, the blessed lord—as Skanda, wondrous to behold—went to where Rudra was.

sanskrit: viśākhas tu yayau yena devī girivarātmajā śākho yayau ca bhagavān vāyumūrtir vibhāvasum naigameṣo 'gamad gaṅgāṃ kumāraḥ pāvakaprabhaḥ
english: Viśākha went to where the goddess, daughter of the best of mountains, was; and the blessed Śākha, in the form of the Wind, went to the Fire; while Naigameṣa, the youth bright as flame, went to Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: sarve bhāsvaradehās te catvāraḥ samarūpiṇaḥ tān samabhyayur avyagrās tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: All four of them, with shining bodies and alike in form, drew near them unhurried; and this was as a wonder to behold.

sanskrit: hāhākāro mahān āsīd devadānavarakṣasām tad dṛṣṭvā mahad āścaryam adbhutaṃ romaharṣaṇam
english: A great cry of wonder arose from the gods, dānavas, and rākṣasas as they beheld that mighty marvel, wondrous and hair-raising.
